newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Travel between Yugoslavia and Croatia eased.
newsitem.headline: Travel between Yugoslavia and Croatia eased.

text.p: Rump Yugoslavia and Croatia fixed a visa problem that was limiting travel between the two countries on Friday in another move to shore up their recently normalised relations.
The agreement was reached during a meeting between Yugoslav and Croatian interior ministers Vukasin Jokanovic and Ivan Jarnjak in Belgrade, Yugoslav news agency Tanjug reported.
Passenger traffic between the two countries was virtually non-existent until August when they agreed to restore diplomatic relations on an ambassadorial level.

The few people who wanted to travel between Yugoslavia and Croatia had to do so via Hungary. The two countries issued visas in the Hungarian capital Budapest since they had no embassies or consulates in the respective capitals Belgrade and Zagreb.
They normalised relations last August after five years of hostility sparked by a six-month war in 1991 when Serbs in Croatia rebelled against its seccession from former Yugoslavia.
Jokanovic said that the two sides agreed to cooperate in fighting international terrorism and crime "because no country can be isolated in this struggle".
"The normalisation of Yugoslav-Croatian relations has laid grounds for cooperation between the two countries' interior ministries," he said.
